544458.name: Shree Refrigerations Ltd
544458.one_line: Shree Refrigerations is a genuinely qualified, genuinely differentiated naval HVAC&R manufacturer with a real approval moat, a repaired balance sheet and an order book of Rs 270.8 cr - but it has produced negative cumulative operating cash flow over five years, its order book fell 17% in the half in which revenue doubled, its managerial remuneration breached Section 197 in a record-profit year, and at Rs 375 the price sits 71.5% to 89.8% above every scenario in our DCF while the reverse DCF implies about 84% annual sales growth for five years against 19.8% in the base case.

544669.name: Admach Systems Ltd
544669.one_line: Admach Systems is a genuine, newly listed Pune special-purpose-machine and NDT builder with credible customers, zero debt and real defence, nuclear and European-partner optionality, but it has never generated free cash flow, its working-capital cycle has widened every year for five years, its most recent half was its weakest on margin in two years, and at Rs 475 the shares trade above every value benchmark our evidence supports - including the bull case - on a price that implies roughly 57% compound sales growth for five years against management's own Rs 200 cr facility ceiling.

544773.name: Merritronix Ltd
544773.one_line: Merritronix is a genuinely qualified, fast-growing but cash-consuming defence-and-aerospace contract assembler whose operating record is better than its cash statement and whose Rs 380 share price sits above every scenario in our DCF, including the bull case at Rs 147.7.

544823.name: Devson Catalyst Ltd
544823.one_line: Devson Catalyst is a real, low-debt, approval-gated niche maker of guard-bed catalysts, adsorbents and ceramic support media, but its FY26 margin jump leaned on an inventory build, cash conversion is weak, core disclosures are missing, and at Rs 319 every modelled DCF value sits 67-87% below the price and implies about 63% annual sales growth for five years.

ABB.name: ABB India Ltd
ABB.one_line: ABB India is a genuinely high-quality, debt-free, AAA-rated electrification and automation franchise whose orders have inflected to a record Rs 11,900 crore backlog, but whose margin has compressed for six straight quarters on drivers management itself describes as largely permanent, and whose share price implies about 82% annual sales growth for five years against 11.6% in our base-case DCF.

ACCENTMIC.name: Accent Microcell Ltd
ACCENTMIC.one_line: Accent Microcell owns one genuinely high-return asset - the Dahej SEZ export unit at a 23.3% PBIT margin and roughly 38% pre-tax return on segment capital - but roughly half of FY26's 31.9% revenue growth was bought in at 4-5% margins, a third of the balance sheet sits in a plant that has missed four commissioning dates, and at Rs 682 the price implies about 62% compound sales growth for five years against bear, base and bull fair values of Rs 95.4, Rs 186.4 and Rs 271.9.

BEL.name: Bharat Electronics Ltd
BEL.one_line: Bharat Electronics is a structurally advantaged, debt-free defence-electronics incumbent whose 29% operating margin and 36% ROCE are real but have converted into cash at only 0.44x reported profit over three years, while the share price sits 67.5% to 83.7% above every fair value our DCF model produces across all scenarios and sensitivities.

CFF.name: CFF Fluid Control Ltd
CFF.one_line: CFF Fluid Control is a qualified, profitable, low-debt naval subsystem supplier with a ~Rs 551 cr order book, but its reported profits have not converted to cash and the Rs 1,104 share price sits far above even the bull-case DCF value of Rs 262.5, implying ~96% annual growth that no disclosed evidence supports.

CUMMINSIND.name: Cummins India Ltd
CUMMINSIND.one_line: Cummins India is a debt-free, 40%-ROCE engine and genset franchise whose FY26 record was genuine but whose growth has narrowed onto data centres and three unnamed customers, whose margin has already turned down in Q1 FY27, and whose Rs 5,100 share price sits far above every fair value our DCF model can support.

FILATEX.name: Filatex India Ltd
FILATEX.one_line: Filatex is a well-run, near-net-cash, cash-generative Indian polyester filament yarn converter whose revenue has been flat to down for four years and whose entire growth case rests on an uncommissioned Rs 690 cr capex programme and an unproven chemical recycling platform - trading at Rs 90.4 against a base-case DCF value of Rs 32.5 and a bull-case value of Rs 71.6, with the screened growth rates that justify the price being artifacts of a five-year gap in the data.

FLUIDOM.name: Fluidomat Ltd
FLUIDOM.one_line: Fluidomat, a debt-free, cash-rich niche maker of fluid couplings, has made a real FY25 step-up to about Rs 72 cr of revenue at margins above 30%, but FY26 was flat, order intake is not visible and receivables are climbing, while the Rs 750 share price sits above every scenario in our FY23-based DCF (reverse DCF about 86% implied growth), so the market is pricing a growth resumption the documents do not yet evidence.

GRSE.name: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd
GRSE.one_line: GRSE is executing better than at any point in its 92-year history - Rs 7,507 cr of trailing revenue, an 11%+ FY26 margin and 43% ROCE - but it is doing so by liquidating a backlog it has not replaced for five quarters, converting -0.60x of three-year profit into operating cash, and trading at roughly four times the base-case fair value in our DCF model, which requires about 65% annual sales growth for five years to justify today's price.

HAL.name: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd
HAL.one_line: HAL is a certified monopoly overhaul annuity attached to a Rs 46,192 cr customer-funded treasury, wrapped around a new-build programme that has delivered none of the 35 fighters contractually due across three years - and its share price of Rs 4,905 implies about 62.5% annual sales growth for five years against a nine-year record of 7.0%, a gap that no scenario, discount rate or sensitivity cell in our model can bridge.

HBLENGINE.name: HBL Engineering Ltd
HBLENGINE.one_line: HBL Engineering is a high-quality, debt-free, approval-moated industrial whose FY26 step-change in revenue and margin came almost entirely from one railway safety programme in its execution phase, and whose share price at Rs 760 sits above the fair value implied by every scenario in our model, with the reverse DCF requiring about 59% annual sales growth for five years.

INOXINDIA.name: Inox India Ltd
INOXINDIA.one_line: INOX India is a genuinely certified, net-cash global cryogenic engineering franchise with a record Rs 1,686 cr order book, but its entire FY26 growth came from exports while domestic revenue stood still, its profit converts to cash at 0.45x, and at Rs 1,979 the price implies roughly 77% annual sales growth for five years against a 14% base case and 9% delivered in Q1 FY27.

KSB.name: KSB Ltd
KSB.one_line: KSB Limited is a debt-free, 25%-ROCE pump and valve franchise with a genuine 49-year nuclear qualification moat, but its domestic revenue grew 2% in CY2025, H1 CY2026 profit fell about 20%, it has converted only 49 paise of every rupee of five-year profit into operating cash, and at Rs 803 it trades 78% to 94% above every fair value our DCF model produces.

MAZDOCK.name: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd
MAZDOCK.one_line: Mazagon Dock is a genuinely scarce state-qualified submarine and destroyer builder whose two flagship programmes have just been fully delivered, leaving an order book down 60% in four years with half of it sitting on already-delivered ships, cash conversion at 0.02x profit over three years, and a share price that sits 63-86% above every scenario in our DCF - so the investment question is not the quality of the yard but when the Ministry of Defence signs the next submarine contract and at what margin.

MODISONLTD.name: Modison Ltd
MODISONLTD.one_line: Modison has a real but narrow HV contact franchise. Its FY26-TTM earnings jump coincides with a silver-driven inventory build, three years of negative operating cash flow and rising debt, so the Rs 468 price, which sits above even the bull DCF value of Rs 143.1, is effectively a bet that a five-quarter-old ~19% EBITDA margin is permanent.

NATIONALUM.name: National Aluminium Company Ltd
NATIONALUM.one_line: NALCO is a genuinely integrated, effectively debt-free bauxite-to-metal producer earning cycle-peak margins it does not control, trading within 3% of the base-case DCF value while every scenario in that model - including the bear case - assumes an EBITDA margin at or above the top of its own ten-year distribution.

POWERINDIA.name: Hitachi Energy India Ltd
POWERINDIA.one_line: Hitachi Energy India is an entrenched, debt-free, AAA-rated Indian grid-equipment incumbent with a Rs 32,222 cr order backlog covering about 3.5 years of revenue and a margin that has tripled in three years - but order intake has been flat for two years, roughly nine-tenths of its export revenue appears to be intra-group, Rs 602 cr of royalty and group charges equal 45.6% of pre-tax profit, and at 117x trailing earnings the price sits far above every fair value our DCF produces.

QLINE.name: Q-Line Biotech Ltd
QLINE.one_line: Q-Line Biotech's move into reagent manufacturing is real and its FY26 margin gains are audited, but about two-thirds of revenue goes to a promoter partnership, three years of profit have not turned into cash, and at Rs 726 the share trades above even our model bull value of Rs 382.9 while implying about 45% annual sales growth for five years.

SIKA.name: Sika Interplant Systems Ltd
SIKA.one_line: A genuinely debt-free, 35%-ROCE, certification-backed Bengaluru aerospace and defence supplier whose accounts show a predominantly trading, import-dependent business with a shrinking order book and no customer disclosure - trading at a price that our reverse DCF says requires 77.6% annual sales growth for five years against a 15.6% base case, and above every fair value the model produces.

SIMPLEXCAS.name: Simplex Castings Ltd
SIMPLEXCAS.one_line: Simplex Castings has delivered a real, third-party-corroborated turnaround - FY26 revenue of Rs 202.90 cr, PAT of Rs 21.26 cr and gearing down to 0.47x - but its growth story rests on uncontracted targets (Rs 300 cr FY27, Rs 500 cr FY28, a railway vertical still at zero revenue) while the disclosure needed to value the equity is missing, with no audited FY26 accounts, no segment or customer data, an unreconciled share count and four of five rating agencies recording the company as not submitting information.

TRITURBINE.name: Triveni Turbine Ltd
TRITURBINE.one_line: Triveni Turbine is a debt-free, high-return niche engineering franchise with a genuine qualification-and-technology moat, but FY26 growth came entirely from one near-zero-margin turnkey project, order booking and cash conversion both went backwards, and at Rs 568 the shares sit 64% to 85% above every scenario in our DCF - a price that implies about 58% annual sales growth for five years against a nine-year actual of 12.7%.

VIMTALABS.name: Vimta Labs Ltd
VIMTALABS.one_line: Vimta Labs is a well-financed, cleanly accounted contract research and testing business with two genuinely regulator-conferred franchises and a four-year record of margin and export expansion, but it discloses neither segments, order book, customer concentration nor utilisation, its largest shareholder at 19.72% is a competitor it names on its own calls, and every fair value our model produces sits more than 80% below the traded price.
